newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian share close mixed, preferred shares rise.
newsitem.headline: Russian share close mixed, preferred shares rise.

text.p: Leading Russian shares closed mixed on Thursday in quiet trade with preferred shares rising, traders said.
"Preferred shares rose quite well today," said Andrei Ippolitov, corporate securities director at IK Prospekt. "In the West they are setting up special funds for Russian preferred shares."
He said Western investors considered Russian preferred shares attractive as they pay high dividends.
Surgutneftegaz and UES were gainers of the day among preferred stocks.
Surgutneftegaz preferred rose to $0.253 from $0.240 at Wednesday close and UES preferred rose to $0.0540 from $0.0472.
Ippolitov said that Surgutneftegaz preferred rose in reaction to a big fall they experienced after Surgut Holding said it had acquired a whole new issue of Surgutneftegaz share issue.
Pavel Gronbjerg, co-head equities trader at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, said news about the forthcoming UES Eurobond sparked interest to UES preferred shares.
Privatisation minister Alfred Kokh said UES would issue Eurobonds convertible into 7.5 percent of its shares in the first half of December.
Nizhnevatovskneftegaz was one of the gainers among ordinary shares after investors realised that it was most undervalued among all oil shares, Ippolitov said.
Nizhnevartovskneftegaz rose to $5.95 from $5.50 on August 9, when the share was last traded.
Norilsk Nickel fell to $6.38 from $6.42 at Wednesday's close, UES was $0.0817 after $0.0809, Rostelekom edged up to $2.56 from $2.55 and Mosenergo fell to $0.955 from $0.958.
